text: Instruction: Explain to a new engineer why the service retries with exponential backoff instead of immediately. Response: Immediate retries against an overloaded dependency amplify the overload — every failed call is replaced by several more. Exponential backoff spaces retries out so the dependency gets room to recover, and adding jitter prevents synchronized retry storms when many clients fail at the same moment. The combination turns a thundering herd into a trickle the service can absorb.

Instruction: Summarize the difference between tensor parallelism and pipeline parallelism in two sentences. Response: Tensor parallelism splits the weight matrices of each layer across devices, so every device participates in every layer and they synchronize with collective operations inside the forward pass. Pipeline parallelism instead assigns whole contiguous groups of layers to different devices and streams micro-batches through them, trading collective bandwidth for pipeline-bubble overhead.

Instruction: A user asks for the fastest way to deduplicate a 2 TB text corpus. Response: Exact duplicates fall out of a content-hash pass, which is cheap and embarrassingly parallel. Near-duplicates need MinHash signatures over shingled n-grams fed into locality-sensitive hashing, clustering candidates whose estimated Jaccard similarity exceeds your threshold, commonly around 0.85. Run the hash pass first so the expensive LSH stage only sees unique documents.
